FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.2
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_categorise_ruff()` classifies all `F` codes as `DefectCategory.DEAD_CODE` (`if code.startswith("F"): return DefectCategory.DEAD_CODE`). Pyflakes `F821` is "undefined name", which is a critical runtime crash, not dead code. Masking it as dead code leads to incorrect downstream prioritization.
FOLLOW: An undefined name bug will be tagged as DEAD_CODE. The insect brain and immune pipeline will treat it as a low-severity style/cleanup issue rather than a critical code behavioral bug, potentially ignoring it.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Check for critical F-codes explicitly before the prefix match. `if code == "F821": return DefectCategory.TYPE_SAFETY`
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 1.00
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.8
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_create_sandbox` uses `os.path.commonpath(all_paths)` as the base directory for copying files. If all source files are inside a package (e.g., `bench/`), `commonpath` evaluates to that package directory. The files are flattened into `tmpdir` without the package prefix (e.g., `tmpdir/endocrine.py` instead of `tmpdir/bench/endocrine.py`).
FOLLOW: Static analysis tools (pyright/mypy) running in the sandbox will fail to resolve absolute imports like `from bench.dm import...` because the `bench` directory no longer exists in the sandbox root. This introduces artificial type errors, causing `_compute_fix_verdict` to erroneously mark nearly all SAFE fixes as HARMFUL.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Use the project root (current working directory) instead of `commonpath`. Replace `common = os.path.commonpath(all_paths)` with `common = os.getcwd()`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.90
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.3
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_apply_fix_to_source` Strategy 3 regex (`line_pattern`) uses `.+?` and `.+` without `re.DOTALL`. Because the dot metacharacter does not match newlines by default, the regex will fail to capture any replacement blocks where the `old_frag` or `new_frag` spans multiple lines.
FOLLOW: Models frequently output multi-line code blocks in replacements. The regex will silently fail to match them, returning `None`, and `evaluate_fix` will mark the fix `UNEVALUABLE`, leaving the bug unfixed.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Add `re.DOTALL` to `line_pattern` and make the final match non-greedy, bounded by a lookahead: `re.compile(r"[Ll]ines?\s+(\d+)(?:\s*[-–]\s*(\d+))?:\s*(.*?)\s*->\s*(.*?)(?=\n[Ll]ines?|\Z)", re.DOTALL)`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.85
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.4
DESCRIPTION: FIND — In `compute_pacing_signals()`, the response size anomaly check (Check 4) incorrectly hardcodes `signal_type="context_growth"`. 
FOLLOW: This overwrites or conflates the true context growth signal (Check 2). The insect brain relies on distinct `signal_type` values to trigger different mechanical mitigations. Sending a response size anomaly as a context growth signal will trigger the wrong downstream reaction (e.g., degrading relay instead of isolating a broken model).
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Change `signal_type="context_growth"` to `signal_type="response_size_anomaly"` in Check 4.
VERIFIED: TRUE
